narrative.overview: Wordt is a living-room word tournament: the phone is the player's controller and the TV is the shared, display-only arena. Both clients share palette and Barlow typography while using distinct interaction scales. The five user-selected colors are neon chartreuse, icy aqua, frosted mint, stormy teal, and shadow grey. Mint text tint (#C7F2F1) is derived from icy aqua for supporting text on teal and is not an additional selected color.
keyCharacteristics: Chartreuse marks primary actions, active selections, and meaningful game events.
Stormy teal groups game content; frosted mint carries text and letter tiles.
Barlow Condensed carries display moments; Barlow keeps controls and copy clear.
Phone controls remain reachable while TV information reads across the room.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Reserve chartreuse for the next action, active selection, or meaningful game event; do not use it as decoration that competes with game information.

dos: Do keep phone controls reachable and TV information legible at couch distance.
Do keep keyboard focus visible with an icy-aqua outline.
Do pair color with explicit state information and honor reduced-motion preferences.
donts: Don't use chartreuse as body text on light surfaces.
Don't alter game rules, outcomes, room behavior, or server authority through visual styling.
Don't introduce extra palette colors, gradients, or glass effects that compete with game information.
